dedupe_keys.name: ntia internet use survey current population survey computer and internet use supplement

description: The NTIA Internet Use Survey is a supplement to the US Census Bureau's Current Population Survey, sponsored by the National Telecommunications and Information Administration since 1994, that asks about 50,000 households how their members use the internet, at home and elsewhere, which devices they use, what connections the household has and why some do not go online. NTIA publishes public use microdata for every wave, from 1994 to November 2023, in Stata, R, CSV and the raw fixed-width format with Census Bureau technical documentation, and an Analyze Table of about 2.3 MB with estimates and standard errors by state and demographic group that feeds the NTIA Data Explorer's maps, charts and fact sheets. Coverage: the United States, national and state level, waves every one to two years. Format and access: ZIP, RDS and CSV downloads and an interactive explorer, free of charge as a US Government work. Caveats: survey estimates with sampling error; questions change between waves; household reports of connection type, not measured service. Simulation uses: population dependence on home internet and mobile connections by group and state, for social vulnerability and equity weighting of outage impacts. Related records: the ITU ICT statistics give international counterparts; FCC broadband maps show supply, not use.
